Hi Alex / Jamie —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the follow-ups we said we'd do: 

1) Ask: FinServe is requesting a 0-retention option for all PII-containing request payloads (no persistent storage) and a shortened log retention schedule for telemetry (14 days) for the integration pilot.
2) Residency: You need all production inference and logs to reside in us-west-2.
3) Audit: SOC 2 evidence and an incident notification SLA (24 hours) are required for procurement.

Next steps on our side:
- I will check with our security/compliance team about an exception for 0-retention and confirm what parts of the request flow we can make ephemeral.
- Send SOC2 summary and a proposed retention schedule.
- If approved, we'll draft an addendum to include the custom retention schedule and residency terms for pilot.

Can you confirm the following so we align the draft?
- Does 14 days cover all telemetry you need for troubleshooting, or do you need longer for metrics/aggregates?
- Will you require audit logs (who/when) beyond the 14-day window?

I’ll loop Marissa on the technical details.

Hi Camila —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- 0-retention: We need the request body (which may contain PII) to never be written to disk in production. Short-lived in-memory processing and KV-cache are OK as long as they are not persisted to durable storage.
- Logs: 14 days is fine for raw logs; however, we need anonymized aggregates stored for 90 days for trend analysis. Aggregates must have no PII and be verifiably aggregated.
- Residency: yes, us-west-2 only for pilot (and ideally for the first 6 months).
- Audit: procurement will want SOC 2 summary and a redlined DPA/addendum.

If you can provide a proposed exception language and a sample DPA addendum we can route to legal/procurement this week, that would be ideal.

Appreciate you looping in your security lead.

—Alex

Hi Camila / Alex / Jamie —

Thanks — and thanks for the clear asks, Alex. Quick answers and a proposed path forward: 

What we can commit for a pilot (us-west-2):
- 0-retention for PII in request payloads: We can configure the runtime to avoid writing request payloads to durable storage. Requests will be processed in-memory; KV cache entries related to user request payloads can be configured to be in-memory only and evicted immediately post-response. We will provide a short technical appendix describing where data may transiently exist (in-memory, GPU RAM, ephemeral instance memory) and attest that no application-level persistent store will be used for request bodies.
- Raw logs: We can set raw logs to 14 days retention for the pilot (we will redact PII from logs by default).
- Aggregates: We can produce anonymized aggregates stored for 90 days. We will share an aggregation methodology doc to show how PII is removed prior to storage.

Caveats / technical notes:
- Retries and async queueing: If you enable retries or long-running async jobs, we may need to persist small retry metadata; we can minimize and encrypt it. We recommend disabling long retry windows or routing them to a separate queue with its own retention policy for the pilot.
- KV caches: We will configure them as ephemeral for your pilot; however, persistent KV for performance is an opt-in tradeoff (we can keep it off).

Evidence and docs attached: SOC2_summary.pdf (high-level points), and a draft custom-retention-schedule.xlsx with proposed field-level retention. I’ve also attached a redwood-data-processing-addendum.docx (DPA addendum draft) with suggested language for the 0-retention exception and residency commitment.

Proposed next steps:
1) FinServe review: Alex/Jamie to confirm aggregate requirements and any legal redlines to the DPA addendum.
2) Technical sync: 30-min call tomorrow to confirm runtime flags and confirm that retries/async are acceptable.
3) Legal: if FinServe approves language, we can send a redline-ready addendum for procurement this week.

If that works I’ll open a HubSpot note and share the DocuSign link for the addendum once we have sign-off.

—Marissa Cole
